ci_support_linux_64_.yaml:
channel_sources:
- conda-forge
channel_targets:
- conda-forge main
docker_image:
- quay.io/condaforge/linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10
python_min:
- '3.11'

about.description:
Photo Tagger is a command-line helper that asks a vision-language model to
analyze your photos and writes Lightroom-compatible metadata. By default it
keeps your originals untouched by creating XMP sidecar files, but it can
embed the updates directly into each photo with --embed-in-photo.

It requires a running Ollama or LM Studio server that hosts a vision-language
model, and the ExifTool binary available on PATH. The optional photo-tagger-gui
package adds a PySide6 desktop frontend (the `photo-tagger gui` command).
about.summary: CLI tool to describe photos and add keywords using AI

name: photo-tagger
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "0.8.0"
  # photo-tagger needs Python >= 3.14, higher than conda-forge's global
  # python_min, so override it here and reference ${{ python_min }} below.
  python_min: "3.14"

recipe:
  name: photo-tagger
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/p/photo-tagger/photo_tagger-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: ece916b1cdf60339e23d7c7827038977df88f8dd4e807382da3b7f34a34523b9

build:
  number: 0
  noarch: python

outputs:
  - package:
      name: photo-tagger
    build:
      script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
      python:
        entry_points:
          # 0.6.0 wraps the cyclopts app in main() so unhandled crashes can send an anonymous
          # crash beacon before the traceback surfaces.
          - photo-tagger = photo_tagger.main:main
    requirements:
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - uv-build >=0.11.28,<1.0.0
        - pip
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - cyclopts >=4.24.0
        - filelock >=3.32.5
        - httpx2 >=2.12.0
        - loguru >=0.7.3
        # photo-tagger talks to every backend through pydantic-ai's OpenAI model,
        # which imports the `openai` package. The conda-forge `pydantic-ai` ships
        # only the slim core (no model extras), so depend on `openai` explicitly.
        - openai >=2.29.0
        - pillow >=12.3.0
        - pydantic >=2.13.5
        - pydantic-ai >=2.37.0
        - pyexiftool >=0.5.6
        - rawpy >=0.27.1
        - rich >=15.0.0
        - tomlkit >=0.15.1
        # photo-tagger shells out to the `exiftool` binary at runtime to read/write
        # metadata, so depend on it directly (not just via pyexiftool).
        - exiftool
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - photo_tagger
          pip_check: true
          python_version:
            - ${{ python_min }}.*
            - "*"
      - requirements:
          run:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        script:
          - photo-tagger --help

  - package:
      name: photo-tagger-gui
    build:
      # Metapackage: the GUI code ships in the photo-tagger package; this output
      # only pins it together with PySide6 (the `gui` extra) so `photo-tagger
      # gui` works without a separate `pip install`. No build step of its own.
      noarch: python
    requirements:
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("photo-tagger", exact=true) }}
        - pyside6 >=6.11.2
    tests:
      - requirements:
          run:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        script:
          # Import the Qt frontend headlessly to prove PySide6 is wired up.
          env:
            QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
          content:
            - python -c "import photo_tagger.gui"

about:
  summary: CLI tool to describe photos and add keywords using AI
  description: |
    Photo Tagger is a command-line helper that asks a vision-language model to
    analyze your photos and writes Lightroom-compatible metadata. By default it
    keeps your originals untouched by creating XMP sidecar files, but it can
    embed the updates directly into each photo with --embed-in-photo.

    It requires a running Ollama or LM Studio server that hosts a vision-language
    model, and the ExifTool binary available on PATH. The optional photo-tagger-gui
    package adds a PySide6 desktop frontend (the `photo-tagger gui` command).
  license: MIT
  license_file: LICENSE
  homepage: https://juliobs.com/projects/photo-tagger/
  repository: https://github.com/jbsilva/photo-tagger
  documentation: https://github.com/jbsilva/photo-tagger

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - jbsilva
